findings.title: D6's degraded-parse premise does not match the parser, and its fix would mislabel every derived-verdict artifact
findings.description:
D6 describes "a PASS parsed with `fallback_used=True` (verdict read, findings not)". The parser cannot produce that state.
- `parsers.py:1023-1025` sets `fallback_used` in the mismatch branch only for `verdict in (CONCERNS, FAIL) and not findings`.
- The only other setter is the derived branch (`parsers.py:991-993`). There the verdict comes from findings, so findings are non-empty and `verdict_source` is `DERIVED`.
- So a PASS with `fallback_used=True` always has findings, and today's `if result.findings:` branch wins.

Making the notice render "whenever `fallback_used` is set, after any findings" (`persistence.py:528`, `review.py:187`) changes every derived-verdict artifact, not only capped ones. It also prints text that is false in that case:
- The notice reads "A verdict of PASS was parsed, but no findings could be extracted."
- The terminal reads "verdict parsed, findings did not."

SC7 (line 292) describes a case that does not occur as stated. The design should also account for the existing tests that pin this rendering: `fallback_used` appears 16 times in `tests/review/test_persistence.py` and `tests/cli/test_review_format.py`.

Separately, `impose_diff_coverage` overwrites `verdict_source` from `DERIVED` to `IMPOSED`. That drops the #97 provenance the slice-919 contract exists to keep. D5 doesn't say whether that is intended.

findings.title: D4 treats `None` ("not reported") as zero, contradicting the design's own convention and the provider code
findings.description:
D4 uses `(tool_calls_made or 0) - (failed_tool_calls or 0)` and says `None` means "no tools offered". Line 216 states the opposite rule: "`None` means not reported… `is None` checks, never `or 0`, for counts". The code shows `None` has two causes:
- **No tools offered:** `sdk/agent.py:188` and `openai/agent.py:565` stamp tool telemetry only when `_tools_given` is non-empty.
- **Provider stamps nothing:** the Codex provider reports no telemetry at all.

For a provider that stamps nothing, the rule cannot know whether a native read happened. It will still cap a truncated PASS. That may be acceptable, but the design should say so and use the right justification.

SC4 also relies on `failed_tool_calls` to cancel out calls. The SDK counter at `sdk/agent.py:178-180` increments only when a top-level stream message is a `ToolResultBlock`. The design does not verify that this fires for real SDK streams; the SDK normally nests result blocks inside a user message. If it never fires, SDK failures read as 0 and "every read failed" is not detected on the SDK path. The design should verify or note this, since the unit tests for the cap would hand-set the counts.

findings.title: A third silent no-diff path is unhandled: `_run_git_diff` returning `None`
findings.description:
The design names two diff-loss paths: truncation and the total-limit skip. At `review_client.py:420-424`, `_run_git_diff` returns `None` on a non-zero git exit, an `OSError`, or whitespace-only output. In those cases nothing is injected and the model sees no diff. `run_review_with_profile` pre-checks the file list with a separate git call (`_run_git_diff_filenames`, line 110), so the second call can fail independently.

D2 says the key is "always written" when a diff was part of the review. D1 and D3 define `DiffInjection` only for the added and skipped-by-budget cases. As written, this case either yields `diff_injection=None`, which reads as "no diff, no key", or `diffTruncated: false`. Both claim the model saw everything. This is the same class as #135, so the design should record it as `injected_chars=0` or fail the run.

findings.title: Wrong claims about existing call sites
findings.description:
Step 2 says to "Update its two `review_client` call sites". There is one: `review_client.py:154`. `_truncate` has two callers, `_add_injection` (line 376) and `builders/code.py:60`, and the design correctly keeps its signature.

The listed direct callers also include `test_injection_decision.py`. That file never calls `_inject_file_contents`; line 283 is a comment. It exercises the function through `run_review_with_profile`.

The real breakage is bigger than listed. `test_content_injection.py` has about 22 call sites that treat the return value as a string. `test_review_client.py:224` patches `_inject_file_contents` with `side_effect=lambda p, *a, **k: p`, and that returns a `str`. Tuple-unpacking it at the call site will raise. An implementer working from the design's list will under-scope step 2.

findings.title: Scope is heavier than the slice plan entry requires
findings.description:
The plan entry (900-slices:440-444) asks for four things:
- record truncation;
- cap a truncated, unread PASS;
- stamp the answering model, with `requestedModel` on difference;
- decide what counts as "differs".

The design adds mechanisms the requirement does not need. Each of these can be cut or deferred:
- **Plural `answering_models` plumbing (D12).** It runs through metadata, `TurnCapture` folding, `ReviewResult`, JSON, two Run Digest line variants and a multi-model WARNING. A last-answering-model value plus WARNING on a change meets the requirement. The list can come later if a consumer asks.
- **New `models/snapshot.py`.** A module for one roughly 10-line predicate, justified by adjacency to `aliases.py`. It can live beside the review code that uses it.
- **Live capture across four profiles (walkthrough step 6, D9, Risk).** This is a pre-merge task that depends on credentials the operator may not have. It makes the correctness of SC10 conditional on external state. Reduce it to a documented follow-up for profiles that produce a false substitution.
- **D7 and D13.** These are rationale sections for things the slice does not do. The Excluded list already carries them.
- **Model checks on every JSON key.** `model_substituted` is derivable from `requested_model` and `answering_models` and duplicates D9 logic, which D10 itself argues consumers shouldn't reimplement.

findings.title: D10 re-keys metrology judge identity for existing data with no migration or detection
findings.description:
`metrology/identity.py:329-333` builds `JudgeConfigId(model=str(frontmatter["aiModel"]))`. The design accepts that OpenAI-direct judges move from `gpt-5` to `gpt-5-2025-08-07` "once". It does not say what happens to calibration evidence already accumulated under the old id. The code's own docstring (`identity.py:296-301`) records that re-keying "resets accumulated evidence back to zero" as the failure that slice 322 designed against.

The identity also becomes unstable whenever the provider's alias moves to a new snapshot. That is arguably correct, but it is a standing behavior change to a store owned by another slice. The design should state the consequence for existing graduated configs, or keep `aiModel` stable and carry the snapshot elsewhere. Today this is listed under "Provides to Other Slices" as a benefit.

findings.title: Walkthrough steps that cannot run as written, and one leaves persistent state
findings.description:
- **Step 6.** It says "for each profile (sdk, openai, openrouter, local)", but the only command shown is `sq review slice 927 --model sonnet`. That alias resolves to `claude-sonnet-5` on the sdk profile (`models.toml:45-47`). No command selects the other profiles, so the step as written cannot capture D9's ids for them.
- **Step 1.** It runs `sq config set review.max_file_size_bytes 20000 --project`, which writes the project config. Steps 2-4 depend on it and only step 5 unsets it. An abort between steps, or a failure in 2-4, leaves the repo's review cap at 20 KB. The design should add a cleanup path or use an environment or per-invocation override.
- **Step 4.** `sq run review 927` is checked only for "if the model made no successful tool calls". Whether the pause appears depends on live model behavior, so it is not a deterministic check of Part B on the pipeline path. SC4's pipeline half is unproven by the walkthrough.

findings.title: The PR comment is a rendering surface the design does not cover
findings.description: `review/pr_comment.py:38-64` posts `result.verdict` and `result.model` to a GitHub PR. After this slice it will show the capped verdict and the synthetic finding, via `structured_findings`. It will show the answering model without any substitution marker, and it has no truncation line. The data-flow diagram and "parity is structural" claim list only three sinks. State whether the comment is intentionally left alone. `result.model` will change meaning there silently.

findings.title: `judge-findings-addressed` records the requested model in its leg result
findings.description: `review/addressed/judge.py:111-134` stores `model=model_id` (the requested id) on `JudgeLegResult`. The leg runs through `run_review_with_profile`, but the design says only that `ActionResult.metadata["model"]` follows the answering model. That leaves a gate judge that still reports the requested id.

findings.title: SDK model stamping is skipped whenever the result message translates to nothing
findings.description: The design stamps answering models "next to `stop_reason`". That stamp sits behind `if isinstance(sdk_msg, ResultMessage) and translated:` (`sdk/agent.py:183`). When the result translates to no `Message`, the model is not stamped. The Run Digest line from D11 would then read "not reported by provider", which is untrue for the SDK. The design does not address this.
